Join us in building the future of finance.

Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

About the team + role

We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards.

The Brokerage Finance & Strategy team supports the largest P&L at Robinhood. We oversee all financial aspects of Robinhood's core trading and net interest products in Brokerage, including equities, options, margin lending, securities lending, uninvested cash and more across self-directed, managed, and institutional accounts. We also serve as the finance partner to Robinhood's Platforms organizations: Customer Experience, Customer Trust & Safety, Financial Crimes, and Fraud Operations. These volume-driven teams protect our customers and keep the platform running for every business at Robinhood, and their scope reaches well beyond Brokerage.

As the Finance & Strategy Senior Manager for Platforms, you will be the senior finance lead and primary thought partner to the leaders of these organizations. You will own the end-to-end financial picture for teams whose cost base moves with customer volume, market activity, and product launches: translating contact, case, and alert volumes into headcount and vendor capacity, forecasting fraud and operational losses, setting and defending expense and efficiency targets, and shaping the investment case for automation and tooling. You will set the agenda for how Finance supports these businesses, and you will be the person leadership turns to when they need a clear point of view on what a decision costs, what it saves, and what risk it carries.

The ideal candidate has done this before: a seasoned Finance & Strategy or business finance leader who has covered customer-facing, operations-heavy organizations (support, trust and safety, fraud, risk operations) at a fintech or consumer technology company, and who is fluent in volume-based capacity planning and vendor economics. You operate independently, navigate ambiguity, and drive senior business leaders to decisions. This role has regular exposure to Robinhood's executive team and requires exceptional communication skills and executive presence.

This role is based in our Menlo Park, CA office, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week.

At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams.

What you’ll do

  • Serve as the senior finance lead and strategic partner to Platforms leadership across Customer Experience, Customer Trust & Safety, Financial Crimes, and Fraud Operations, owning the full financial view: headcount, BPO and vendor spend, tooling, program costs, and fraud and operational losses
  • Own annual planning, quarterly forecasts, and monthly budget-versus-actuals for a large, volume-driven cost base; build and maintain driver-based models that connect customer and market activity to volumes, capacity, and cost
  • Lead the financial evaluation of major decisions: BPO and vendor renewals, in-house versus outsource, site and geography strategy, automation and AI-driven deflection, and new control or compliance programs
  • Own the forecast and analysis of fraud and operational losses, partnering with Fraud, Risk, and Accounting on loss drivers, reserves, and the tradeoff between loss rates, control tightness, and customer friction
  • Define and track unit economics and efficiency metrics such as cost per contact, cost per case or alert, cost to serve per customer, loss rates, and deflection rates, and set targets that hold up under volume swings
  • Synthesize results into crisp narratives for the CFO, executive team, and board materials; surface risks and opportunities early and recommend actions
  • Partner with Workforce Management, Procurement, Accounting, and People teams so forecasts are grounded in operational reality and actuals are clean and auditable
  • Raise the bar on process: standardize models, automate recurring reporting, and build scalable systems that let Finance keep pace with Robinhood’s growth
  • Mentor and develop more junior members of the Finance & Strategy team and set the standard for analytical rigor and business partnership

What you bring

  • A Bachelor’s degree in business, finance, economics, or a related field; MBA or equivalent experience is a plus
  • 10+ years of progressive finance experience, including meaningful time in FP&A, Finance & Strategy, or business finance roles supporting operating teams
  • Direct experience as the finance partner to customer-facing, volume-driven organizations such as customer support, trust and safety, fraud or risk operations, or similar, including fluency in capacity planning concepts (volume forecasting, handle time, occupancy, shrinkage, in-house versus BPO economics); experience forecasting fraud or operational losses is a strong plus
  • A track record of influencing VP-level and above leaders and driving decisions in fast-moving, ambiguous environments
  • Expert financial modeling skills and the judgment to balance precision with speed; strong grasp of accounting concepts and what makes a model auditable
  • Outstanding written and verbal communication; comfortable presenting to executives and simplifying complex tradeoffs
  • Mastery of Google Sheets, Excel, Google Slides, and PowerPoint; proficiency with SQL and BI tools (Superset, Looker) and planning software (Anaplan) strongly preferred
  • Proven ability to manage multiple competing priorities and drive projects to completion with minimal direction
  • A positive attitude. This means a desire to work hard, be creative, stay curious, and maintain a can-do approach
  • Experience in fintech, brokerage, payments, or consumer technology; exposure to regulated environments is a plus
  • Strong project management skills and the ability to execute collaboratively across complex, matrixed environments

In addition to the base pay range listed below, this role is also eligible for bonus opportunities + equity + benefits.

Base pay for the successful applicant will depend on a variety of job-related factors, which may include education, training, experience, location, business needs, or market demands. The expected base pay range for this role is based on the location where the work will be performed and is aligned to one of 3 compensation zones. Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The Global Sales Development Enablement Team equips Stripe’s Sales Development (SD) and Global Sales Vendor (GSV) teams with the skills, product knowledge, tools, and consistent operating practices they need to perform at their best. We deliver onboarding, ongoing skills development, and program-readiness training across Stripe and our vendor partners.

This APAC role is split roughly 50% SD enablement and 50% GSV enablement. It focuses on delivering high-quality live and virtual training, reinforcing learning through coaching and practice, and applying programs consistently across audiences and locations.

What you’ll do

You will deliver onboarding, recurring enablement, and targeted skill and process training for SD and GSV teams across APAC. You will spend most of your time facilitating sessions, leading practice, and reinforcing learning. You will also work with program owners and subject matter experts to adapt established content for regional needs and use learner feedback to improve training effectiveness. This role is based in Malaysia, with periodic travel within APAC.

Responsibilities

  • Deliver live and virtual onboarding, enablement, and skills workshops for SD and GSV audiences across APAC.
  • Train SD teams on prospecting, qualification, value-based conversations, product fluency, sales tooling, and handoffs. Train GSV teams on program launches, new tools, process changes, and operating-model updates.
  • Run train-the-trainer sessions and delivery calibrations for vendor trainers and team leaders to keep program quality consistent.
  • Adapt established training materials, examples, and role-plays to APAC markets, roles, and sales motions while preserving core program outcomes.
  • Provide coaching, office hours, and practice sessions. Partner with SD leaders, GSV program owners, vendor operations, and subject matter experts to identify capability gaps and plan the right training.
  • Manage the regional training calendar, logistics, and periodic APAC travel. Track attendance, feedback, and assessment results to improve delivery and flag recurring readiness gaps.

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 3+ years of experience in sales enablement, learning and development, sales development, vendor enablement, or a related field.
  • Experience delivering engaging training and workshops in virtual and in-person settings, with a practical understanding of adult learning principles and skills reinforcement.
  • Strong facilitation, communication, and presentation skills, including professional English fluency to explain complex concepts and work with global program owners.
  • Experience supporting sales or sales-development audiences, with an understanding of prospecting, qualification, and coaching.
  • Organised and adaptable, with the ability to build working relationships with managers, program owners, and distributed teams, and to coordinate multiple programs across time zones in changing circumstances.

Preferred qualifications

  • Fluency in an additional language needed to support the APAC markets you will serve (hiring manager to specify the language and reason; see below).
  • Experience supporting SDR/BDR teams, outsourced service providers, vendor partners, or distributed sales teams.
  • Experience in a fast-paced SaaS, financial technology, marketplace, or B2B sales environment.
  • Familiarity with learning management systems, virtual facilitation tools, assessment methods, or training-effectiveness measurement.
  • Certification or formal development in facilitation, coaching, adult learning, or instructional design.

At Stripe, we believe in nurturing talent and providing opportunities for professional growth. If you’re an enthusiastic training facilitator with a passion for empowering Sales Development and Global Sales Vendor teams, we would love to hear from you!

You'll also be able to attend guest speakers and social events, and hopefully get a real sense of what it would be like to work here full-time.

What’s different at Jane Street is that we aren't stuck designing verification tools for legacy languages: we can modify and improve OxCaml, our branch of OCaml, and its development environment to make them well-suited for proof-driven software development.
